原第6–9段连续裁切，包含所有8个填空证据。路线未来阶段按文章当时的计划理解。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1The DART bus rapid transit (BRT) system runs on bus lanes separated from other traffic, mostly in the middle of the road to reduce stoppages. Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

原文片段 · 2'The new buses are much, much better,' says Paulas George, a young IT worker. He takes the bus every day and it has cut his journey time by two-thirds. He says it is not perfect, though, complaining that drivers often refuse to turn on the air conditioning to save fuel.

原文片段 · 3That is not the only problem. A shortage of buses after a serious flood at the main depot during the rainy season means the system is carrying 200,000 people a day - half the expected capacity. Smartcards can't be used as the mechanical readers aren't working either, forcing passengers to buy individual paper tickets for every journey. Each is printed with a scannable QR code, but there are no scanners. Staff stand by the gates and tear tickets as people enter. As a result, queues are considerable at peak times.

原文片段 · 4Morogoro Road to the north-west of the city was phase I of the BRT project. Phases II and III will install bus lanes along Nyerere Road to the south-west and Kilwa Road to the south. Construction on both routes is due to start imminently. Phase IV, towards Bagamoyo in the north, is in the preliminary design stage. 'Much of the city will have access to a world-class transport system within the space of a few years,' says Chris Kost, the Africa director of ITDP (the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy). All phases are being planned to high standards and, once complete, a third of city residents will be within a short walk of the BRT network.

第 19 题 · lanes

designated lanes对应与其他交通隔开的专用道；delays改述stoppages。

bus lanes separated from other traffic ... to reduce stoppages

第 20 题 · boarding

before与prior to同义；答案boarding是付费之后发生的动作。

Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding

第 21 题 · wheelchairs

in wheelchairs改述using wheelchairs；题目限定乘客在什么工具中，不填baby buggies。

the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs

第 22 题 · fuel

temperature control对应air conditioning；reduce ... use对应save，保留名词fuel。

drivers often refuse to turn on the air conditioning to save fuel

第 23 题 · flood

insufficient number对应shortage；severe对应serious；缺车原因是flood。

A shortage of buses after a serious flood at the main depot

第 24 题 · smartcards

some equipment指读卡器，空格问不能使用的东西，因此填smartcards而非readers。

Smartcards can't be used as the mechanical readers aren't working

第 25 题 · gates

人工撕票的地点是gates；tickets在题面已给，不能重复填入。

Staff stand by the gates and tear tickets as people enter

第 26 题 · queues

As a result, queues are considerable at peak times

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这一部分先讲快速公交为什么能提高通行效率与可达性，再用乘客体验和设备故障说明设计与运行的差别，最后交代扩建计划。便利来自专用车道、提前检票和无台阶车辆等具体安排，也依赖车辆、票务和维护正常运作。

原文片段 · 1

The DART bus rapid transit (BRT) system runs on bus lanes separated from other traffic, mostly in the middle of the road to reduce stoppages. Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

专用车道与其他车辆分隔，减少公交受混合交通阻塞的机会；购票和检票放在上车之前，可以减少登车环节的拖延。无台阶车辆让轮椅使用者及推婴儿车的人更容易使用线路。accessible 在这里是实际能进入和使用，不只是知道线路在哪里。

原文片段 · 2

'The new buses are much, much better,' says Paulas George, a young IT worker. He takes the bus every day and it has cut his journey time by two-thirds. He says it is not perfect, though, complaining that drivers often refuse to turn on the air conditioning to save fuel.

乘客 Paulas 的通勤时间缩短了三分之二，但司机为节油不开空调使体验打了折扣。个人评价同时含有改善和不满，though 承接这种转折。原文描述的是这名乘客的经历，不能将相同降幅推给每一位乘客。

原文片段 · 3

That is not the only problem. A shortage of buses after a serious flood at the main depot during the rainy season means the system is carrying 200,000 people a day - half the expected capacity. Smartcards can't be used as the mechanical readers aren't working either, forcing passengers to buy individual paper tickets for every journey. Each is printed with a scannable QR code, but there are no scanners. Staff stand by the gates and tear tickets as people enter. As a result, queues are considerable at peak times.

洪水损坏车库后的车辆短缺使运量只有预期的一半；读卡器和扫码器问题又迫使乘客每次买纸票、工作人员手撕票。技术功能存在于票面或系统设计中，却未真正发挥作用，因此高峰排队明显。That 回接空调问题，说明后面还有更多运行困难。

原文片段 · 4

Morogoro Road to the north-west of the city was phase I of the BRT project. Phases II and III will install bus lanes along Nyerere Road to the south-west and Kilwa Road to the south. Construction on both routes is due to start imminently. Phase IV, towards Bagamoyo in the north, is in the preliminary design stage. 'Much of the city will have access to a world-class transport system within the space of a few years,' says Chris Kost, the Africa director of ITDP (the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy). All phases are being planned to high standards and, once complete, a third of city residents will be within a short walk of the BRT network.

叙述从当前故障转向分期扩建：第一期已有线路，第二、三期即将施工，第四期尚在初步设计。完成后约三分之一居民能步行短距离接入网络，是带条件的未来覆盖描述。不同阶段不能都理解成已经建好并投入使用。

词语与搭配

prior to boarding

在上车之前

prior to 比 before 稍正式；to 是介词，后接 boarding，说明购票检票发生的顺序。

accessible to people using wheelchairs

轮椅使用者能够使用

be accessible to 指对某群体可进入、可使用；这里有无台阶设计作为具体支撑。

half the expected capacity

预期运载能力的一半

expected 标明比较基准是预期值，不是原有实际客流量。

within a short walk of

在步行很短距离即可到达……的范围内

常用来描述住宅与车站、服务设施的接近程度；原文用于尚待完成的线路网络。

句子精读

Ticket purchase and control takes place at stations prior to boarding and the buses are step-free, which means the entire route is accessible to people using wheelchairs or who are travelling with baby buggies.

购票和检票都在乘客上车前于车站进行，而且公交车没有台阶，这意味着轮椅使用者或推着婴儿车出行的人都能使用整条线路。

control 在票务语境中是检票。and 连接车站流程与车辆设计，which means 引出无障碍结果。using wheelchairs 和 who are travelling with baby buggies 都修饰 people，分别列出受益人群；引文保留原文形式。

All phases are being planned to high standards and, once complete, a third of city residents will be within a short walk of the BRT network.

各期工程都正在按照高标准规划；待工程完成后，全市三分之一的居民步行很短距离就能到达快速公交网络。

are being planned 表示正在规划。once complete 是省略结构，意思是这些建设完成以后，并不修饰居民。will be 与 once 一起把覆盖率限定为未来完工后的状态。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

accessible to people using wheelchairs

便于轮椅使用者使用

用于说明公共交通替代方案应照顾不同乘客；需配合无台阶入口、站台等具体设计。

用于写作：交通题中的替代方式不只是增加车辆，还包括让不同人群能实际使用。

within a short walk of

距……很近，步行即可到达

说明住房与公交网络的空间联系；是否足够近应由实际布局支持。

用于写作：直接用于比较高层住宅的条件：密度优势需要交通可达性支持。 · 用于写作：说明公交替代汽车所需的接近性与可靠性，连接设施安排和出行选择。

Rethinking the Past · 艺术年代、研究争议与脑容量未作答观点判断 YNNG · 2 段 · 292 词 · 6 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 69, 70 页

保留原第4–5段；第5段跨PDF69–70页已按原句接合，不增删论证。NG已核对整篇文章。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1Art also seems to have been invented by older hominins. We have had evidence for a long time now that Neanderthals painted on cave walls. Even earlier species, such as Homo erectus, may also have made art, for example by engraving patterns on shells. By far the most contentious claim in this area is that Homo naledi made art. H. naledi lived around 250,000 years ago, making it a contemporary of our species. However, it had quite a small brain, typical of older hominins - and was therefore, according to palaeoanthropological dogma, incapable of complex behaviours. Nevertheless, in the Rising Star cave system in South Africa where the H. naledi remains were found, researchers have found what seem to be etchings - resembling rudimentary artwork- on the cave walls, though these have yet to be firmly dated.

原文片段 · 2To say these claims about H. naledi are controversial is to understate the situation. Many experts say the evidence presented so far is completely inadequate to support them. The dispute has only been heightened by the way the results were released, in a non-traditional journal that publishes peer reviews publicly alongside the paper. My views on the H. naledi controversy are complicated. I do think more evidence is needed: in particular with regard to the dating of the etchings. At the same time, I think the species' small brains are a distraction. Palaeoanthropologists got fixated on brain size because it was what they could see: if what you have is skeletons, then all you know about brains are their shapes and sizes. But other properties, such as the brain's internal wiring, are surely equally important and may explain how a species like H. naledi might have been capable of complex behaviours, despite their small brains.

The dispute has only been heightened by the way the results were released

I think the species' small brains are a distraction ... internal wiring ... equally important

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

作者讨论早期人族艺术的证据及 Homo naledi 争议，既要求刻痕年代得到更可靠确认，也反对只凭脑容量判断复杂行为能力。核心张力是证据需要加强，但评估证据的既有框架本身也值得反思。

原文片段 · 1

Art also seems to have been invented by older hominins. We have had evidence for a long time now that Neanderthals painted on cave walls. Even earlier species, such as Homo erectus, may also have made art, for example by engraving patterns on shells. By far the most contentious claim in this area is that Homo naledi made art. H. naledi lived around 250,000 years ago, making it a contemporary of our species. However, it had quite a small brain, typical of older hominins - and was therefore, according to palaeoanthropological dogma, incapable of complex behaviours. Nevertheless, in the Rising Star cave system in South Africa where the H. naledi remains were found, researchers have found what seem to be etchings - resembling rudimentary artwork- on the cave walls, though these have yet to be firmly dated.

对不同物种的证据强度并不相同：尼安德特人壁画已有证据，更早物种制作艺术则以 may 表示可能。关于 Homo naledi 的说法争议最大，因为传统观点把小脑容量与无法进行复杂行为联系起来；洞壁刻痕看似艺术，但仍没有确定年代。contemporary 指与现代人这一物种在时间上并存。

原文片段 · 2

To say these claims about H. naledi are controversial is to understate the situation. Many experts say the evidence presented so far is completely inadequate to support them. The dispute has only been heightened by the way the results were released, in a non-traditional journal that publishes peer reviews publicly alongside the paper. My views on the H. naledi controversy are complicated. I do think more evidence is needed: in particular with regard to the dating of the etchings. At the same time, I think the species' small brains are a distraction. Palaeoanthropologists got fixated on brain size because it was what they could see: if what you have is skeletons, then all you know about brains are their shapes and sizes. But other properties, such as the brain's internal wiring, are surely equally important and may explain how a species like H. naledi might have been capable of complex behaviours, despite their small brains.

争论既涉及证据是否足够，也受到公开同行评议这一发表方式的影响。作者承认需要更强的年代证据，却认为脑容量争论容易分散注意力：骨骼让研究者容易看到形状和大小，内部连接等重要特征反而难以直接得知。最后提出可能解释，没有宣告已经证实 Homo naledi 会创作艺术。

词语与搭配

have yet to be firmly dated

尚未得到可靠断代

have yet to 表示某事截至叙述时尚未完成；dated 在考古语境中指确定年代。

the evidence presented so far

迄今提出的证据

so far 将判断限定在目前可获得的材料，保留以后出现新证据的可能。

with regard to

关于，就……而言

原文把需要更多证据的范围收窄到刻痕年代，而不是笼统否定全部发现。

got fixated on brain size

过于执着于脑容量

fixated on 带有注意力被单一因素占据的意味，是作者对研究倾向的批评。

句子精读

Palaeoanthropologists got fixated on brain size because it was what they could see: if what you have is skeletons, then all you know about brains are their shapes and sizes.

古人类学家过于执着于脑容量，因为这是他们能观察到的东西：如果手头只有骨骼，那么对大脑所能知道的也就只有形状和大小。

because 解释注意力集中于脑容量的原因。冒号后用 if 条件句展开限制；what you have 作主语，all you know about brains 表示所知的全部内容。这里说的是材料可见性如何影响研究视角。

But other properties, such as the brain's internal wiring, are surely equally important and may explain how a species like H. naledi might have been capable of complex behaviours, despite their small brains.

但其他特征，例如大脑内部的连接方式，想必也同样重要，并且可能解释像 Homo naledi 这样的物种为何虽脑容量较小，却仍可能具备复杂行为能力。

such as 插入具体特征，how 从句作 explain 的宾语。may explain 与 might have been 都保留可能性；despite 引出小脑容量这一看似相反的条件。surely 显示作者的判断语气，不把后面的推测变成定论。

Rethinking the Past · 渐进变化与性别预设未作答选择题 / 句尾匹配 · 4 段 · 365 词 · 5 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 70 页

原第6–9段连续裁切；题面sixth/seventh/final paragraph分别对应本片段第1/2/4段。匹配题完整保留A–F。

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文片段 · 1In a sense, we shouldn't be surprised that so many of these behaviours had their origins in older, extinct hominins. Evolution usually works by incremental steps and so does technology. The first birds weren't great at flying, and the first mobile phones weren't great at, well, anything really. The idea that there was a sudden explosion of intelligence and creativity at some point in our evolution isn't inherently ridiculous: sometimes a system hits a tipping point and undergoes runaway change. But there was never that much evidence that human evolution worked this way. Instead, it seems the Neanderthals and many others all walked so we could run.

原文片段 · 2One way or another, the H. naledi story is going to be an example of letting our preconceptions get in the way of the evidence. The same is true for our ideas about gender in prehistory. Archaeology was invented by individuals with now unfashionably patriarchal views about gender, and those notions fed into their research. Today's researchers are trying to unpick this stuff, and there have been some significant steps in recent years.

原文片段 · 3Perhaps the most dramatic was the demolition of 'Man the Hunter'. This was the idea, promoted for decades, that in most prehistoric societies the men went out to hunt and the women looked after the home. However, a meta-analysis published in June 2023 compiled data on several dozen foraging societies and found women hunted in 80 per cent of them. In line with this, it emerged that an ancient spear-throwing tool called an atlatl enables women to launch projectiles at the same speed as men. We have also seen growing evidence of women occupying positions of authority in ancient societies. The Viking queen Thyra may have helped unify Denmark in the 900s. Going further back, an Iberian leader from around 4000 years ago turned out to be female, not male as many had assumed, when proteins in her teeth were analysed.

原文片段 · 4It seems that the more we find out about past societies, the more our preconceptions about the ways society 'has to be' turn out to be wrong. Inequality, authoritarianism and patriarchy aren't inevitable. They're choices, and prehistory shows us that we can choose differently.
